title: EWMA Charts for Per-Tool Anomaly Profiling in Agent Deployments

original_idea.body:
# EWMA Charts for Per-Tool Anomaly Profiling in Agent Deployments

**Problem:** A sabotage often manifests as an unusual pattern for one specific tool; aggregate monitoring washes this out.

**Direction:** Apply per-stream EWMA control charts, one per tool/argument-type. Learn benign bounds from clean trajectories, run sabotage trajectories, and detect which tool-stream fires first and how early. Compare to a single global monitor.

**Why it matters:** Fine-grained, interpretable, real-time tool-usage anomaly detection that localizes abused capability, useful for kill-switch design. Trivial to implement, zero training.

**Relevant context:** EWMA SPC (arXiv:2503.01858); SHADE-Arena 340+ tools (arXiv:2506.15740).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: per-tool anomaly localization aids kill-switch design and early detection in agent deployment.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: EWMA on per-tool streams; trivial to implement, beginner-feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: per-tool chart firing earliness vs global monitor.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Zero-training stats on logged trajectories; labs underweight this fine-grained tooling.

novelty.reasoning: EWMA classic; per-tool control-monitoring application plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: SPC mature; per-tool agent application plausibly open.
